note: Written before any MemConflict generation run. Settings are not tuned on MemConflict; the telarch arm uses the Telarch round-3 pre-registered reference configuration unchanged.

telarch_arm.settings_source: telarch-evals reports/round3-config.json 'reference' block (budget, candidates, per_term, policy, counter, planner, fill_floor, recency, mmr, bridge, resolve_dates, surface_conflicts); encrypt and passthrough_under are TelarchMemory defaults
telarch_arm.unit: one dialogue round: a user turn and the assistant turns that follow it (LongMemEval convention in telarch-benchmarks)

kibisis_plugin_arm.implementation: replica of hermes plugin kibisis-vault KibisisMemoryProvider.prefetch() over a per-persona encrypted vault
kibisis_plugin_arm.write_path: vault.put per dialogue round with the kibisis_remember tool defaults: scope 'default', epistemic_state chosen by the admission gate (auto_gate on)
kibisis_plugin_arm.caveat: The deployed plugin has no automatic write path; storing every round is a benchmark write policy, not plugin behaviour.

control_arm.purpose: rerun on the same hardware to measure drift against the published v5ftc table before comparing Telarch to published rows
control_arm.method: retrieval-frozen replay (benchmark/replay_answers.py) of the published mnemosyne_results_v5ftc.jsonl: every question is re-answered from its stored top-5 Retrieved_Memories on the run hardware with the shared answer contract, then scored by the same judge. SEH@K and log-rank@K are unchanged by construction, so the AA delta against the published v5ftc row isolates answer-model + judge drift from the hardware change.
control_arm.judge_only_check: the published Mnemosyne v5ftc answers are also re-judged unchanged on the run hardware, separating judge drift from answer drift

changes: run_contract.answer_model corrected: the published v5ftc generate manifests run the answer model with thinking ON (THINKING=1, MEMCONFLICT_ENABLE_THINKING=1) and the shared answer_env decoding; the telarch_* presets already set this, only the description said 'thinking off'.
control_arm.method fixed to the retrieval-frozen replay design; a full Mnemosyne pipeline rerun (its embedding and extraction stack) is not part of this run.

run_contract.answer_model: AxionML/Qwen3.5-4B-NVFP4 served by vLLM as qwen3.5-4b, thinking ON, shared answer_env decoding (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5, max_tokens 16384) as in the published v5ftc generate manifests
run_contract.judge: unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-NVFP4 (gemma-4-12b), penalty judge gj12pen, as scored for the published v5ftc rows

disclosures: Hardware differs from the published rows unless run on a Blackwell (SM100/SM120) GPU with native NVFP4; any other GPU is disclosed and calibrated by the Mnemosyne control arm.
Telarch packs up to 8,000 o200k tokens per answer; the published providers mostly inject top-5/6 items. Context size is reported next to every score.
